text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
- CDU leadership board to delay decision on pension reform.
- SPD says finance minister Theo Waigel has distorted tax advantages of tax reform plan. Industry showing increasing support for reform plan.
- FDP watches with concern as old foes of Chancellor Helmut Kohl come together. FDP warns CDU against forming a grand coalition with SPD.
- Slight decline in industry orders recorded in December, as foreign demand in particular drops.
- Lufthansa gets in shape for competition. CEO Juergen Weber pushes pace, new concern structure to be implemented sooner as planned.
- Many newspapers appear in reduced volume due to warn strikes in publishing industry.
- Unemployment reaches post-war record high of 4.6 million in January, analysts say
- Unemployment in Germany reaches new record level in January, analysts forecast level climbing by 450,000 to 4.4 million.
- Customs office uncovers fraud in sale of contaminated German cattle abroad. About 9,000 German cattle with the illness that cannot be transferred to humans illegally exported
